article.xtts.title: Voice Cloner with XTTS v2
article.xtts.subtitle: A zero-shot voice cloning application: import or record voice references, generate speech from text, and choose between multiple variations.
article.xtts.overview.text:
This project uses XTTS v2 to generate a synthetic voice from a short voice sample. The goal is to create a simple application: the user imports or records a few audio references, writes the text to generate, chooses a language, and gets three downloadable versions.

The project mainly focuses on reproducing vocal timbre, meaning the overall sound and character of the voice.
article.xtts.goal.title: Goal
article.xtts.goal.text:
The main goal is to integrate a modern text-to-speech model into a simple local interface. The user does not need to train a model or handle code: they simply provide a few voice references and a text.

This approach makes it possible to quickly experiment with zero-shot voice cloning while keeping the experience lightweight and accessible.
article.xtts.pipeline.title: General workflow
article.xtts.pipeline.text:
The application sends multiple voice samples, a text, and a generation language to XTTS v2. The model uses these elements to produce a new audio clip with a voice similar to the provided references.

To avoid relying on a single output, three variations are generated using slightly different inference settings. The user can then listen to the results and download the version that feels the most convincing.
article.xtts.preprocessing.title: Audio preprocessing
article.xtts.preprocessing.text:
Before generation, each reference audio is automatically prepared. The signal is converted to mono, resampled to 24 kHz, volume-normalized, and trimmed to remove unnecessary silence at the beginning and end of the file.

This step provides the model with cleaner and more consistent samples, which generally improves generation stability.
article.xtts.app.title: Streamlit application
article.xtts.app.text:
The interface is built with Streamlit to remain simple to run locally. Users can either import audio files or record voice samples directly from their microphone.

The application limits the number of references to ten samples in order to keep the workflow clear and lightweight. Added audio files can also be previewed before generation to quickly check their quality.
article.xtts.variants.title: Variant generation
article.xtts.variants.text:
Voice generation can vary depending on inference parameters, so the application produces three versions of the same sentence.

The first version prioritizes stability, the second aims for a balance between naturalness and similarity, and the third gives the model a bit more freedom. This comparison helps select the most convincing result depending on the voice and generated sentence.
article.xtts.limits.title: Limitations
article.xtts.limits.text:
XTTS v2 can produce convincing zero-shot results, but it does not perfectly reproduce a voice. The model may preserve part of the timbre, pitch, and vocal texture, while losing finer details such as accent, pronunciation habits, or highly personal intonations.

Pronunciation also depends heavily on the provided text and selected language. Proper nouns, acronyms, numbers, or foreign words may require a more phonetic spelling to achieve a more natural result.
article.xtts.conclusion.title: Conclusion and future work
article.xtts.conclusion.text:
This project shows how a modern TTS model can be integrated into a small local application. The result is a simple tool for experimenting with voice cloning from only a few audio samples.

Possible improvements mainly include automatic splitting of long sentences, smarter text normalization, and experimenting with an audio-to-audio model — heavier to run and more resource-intensive, but potentially more accurate for certain use cases.
